findings: Each document has a single fixed home region (US or EU) determined at creation by its owning workspace's registered region; EU workspaces are pinned to EU home region for all documents, no per-edit or per-user region selection.

EU residency is enforced as full data-plane isolation, not a policy flag: separate compute clusters, document/CRDT storage, blob storage, KMS/encryption keys, backups, and DR replicas live entirely within EU cloud regions (e.g. eu-west-1 with eu-central-1 as EU-only warm standby), with zero replication or failover path to US infrastructure.

Only a thin global control-plane directory (workspace_id -> home_region mapping, containing no PII or document content) is allowed to be non-regional; all authenticated client connections are proxied at the edge/gateway into the document's home-region cluster based on this lookup, regardless of the physical location of the connecting user.

Real-time collaboration uses a CRDT (sequence CRDT such as RGA/Yjs-style) as the core document model instead of a centrally-sequenced OT server or locking, so concurrent/offline edits merge deterministically without a single global ordering authority and without a cross-region bottleneck.

Perceived sub-200ms latency is achieved via local-first optimistic apply: a user's own keystrokes render instantly against local CRDT state before any network round trip; the 200ms budget is only spent on propagating an edit to other collaborators, which is dominated by same-region intra-cluster latency since the collab hub for a document runs in its home region.

Each region (US, EU) runs an independent real-time collab-server cluster (WebSocket fan-out + in-memory CRDT state + periodic snapshot persistence) that only serves documents whose home region is that region; cross-region collaborators (e.g. a US guest on an EU workspace's doc) connect into the EU hub rather than the doc's state or computation ever being replicated to a US hub.

Audit-event durability is decoupled into two tiers: a synchronous, multi-AZ-replicated regional append-only log (Raft- or Kafka/Kinesis-style) that must durably persist an edit's audit event before the collab server acknowledges the edit as committed, and a separate asynchronous indexing/query consumer that reads off this log — so an outage of the indexing/analytics layer cannot lose events, since the durable log (with 7+ day retention) is the source of truth and gets replayed on recovery.

Audit logs are region-scoped, not centralized: EU audit events are stored and replicated only within EU infrastructure (mirroring the document-data residency boundary), with a federated query layer on top rather than a single global audit index, so audit data itself never violates the EU residency constraint.

Full-region-outage protection for the audit log uses EU-only cross-AZ/cross-region DR replication (e.g. eu-west-1 to eu-central-1) so recovery point is near-zero without ever replicating audit data outside the EU, mirroring the document-storage DR strategy.

Client devices persist unacknowledged edits and their pending audit events locally (e.g. IndexedDB) and only clear them once the server confirms durable write to the regional log; on network partition the collab server withholds a 'committed' ack rather than falsely confirming durability, and the client retries after reconnect, giving a second durability tier that covers the gap between local edit and server-side durable capture.

Observability, telemetry, crash-reporting, and APM pipelines are explicitly region-pinned and scrubbed of document content/PII per region, treating them as a residency leak vector rather than exempting them as 'just logs'.

Semantic merge conflicts (e.g. concurrent delete-vs-edit of the same span) are accepted as a product-level UX tradeoff resolved deterministically by the CRDT's merge semantics (structural no-data-loss guaranteed), rather than treated as a failure of the 'no data loss' constraint, and are surfaced to users via conflict/version indicators rather than silently hidden.

Cross-region collaboration latency for a guest connecting into a foreign-region hub (e.g. a US user on an EU document) is explicitly accepted as a physics-bound degraded case (~80-150ms added RTT) rather than solved architecturally, mitigated only by edge WebSocket termination and delta-compressed CRDT update payloads.
